content.text: I have the structural evidence I need. Writing up.

findings.claim: The corpus's downstream half has no receiver: no Bounded Context exists on this branch, and scenario-assignment has a recorded, unfixed gap for assigning to the lead shop itself — so product-flow's assign→build→verify half cannot execute at all.
findings.evidence: features/feat-typedef-rendering.md:271 and feat-plain-voice-sections.md:124 both state "no Bounded Context exists on this branch" and "contracts — none exist on this branch"; the latter names the gap explicitly: "this is the already-recorded process gap bd lead-ki66p (scenario-assignment lacks a lead-shop-internal path)". basis/processes/product-flow.md steps `assign`→`dispatch`→`build`→`verify` all presuppose a BC shop; `implementation-process` is not a step of product-flow at all (grep: zero references to implementation-process from any process definition). Every recorded assignment tags `@bounded-context:shopsystem-product` — the lead shop — and records "Sent: none".

findings.claim: The session primer compiled into every session — the single highest-leverage governed context — describes the operating flow using four RETIRED processes, and states an absolute rule pointing at one of them.
findings.evidence: .claude/shop/primer.md lines 42–45 name `initiative-check`, `backlog-ordering`, `po-output-check` as product-flow stages; line 66: "deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions." All four carry `status: retired` (basis/processes/: backlog-ordering v5, initiative-check v12, po-output-check v10, stakeholder-presentation v7). There is currently no approved process for delivering anything to the product authority.

findings.claim: 31 approved definitions cite the four retired processes as current, and the lint cannot catch it — link checks verify the file resolves, not that its status is live.
findings.evidence: Approved docs citing retired processes: po-output-check — 11 (incl. basis/artifacts/initiative.md, product-decision-record.md, backlog-order.md, basis/processes/feature-authoring.md, basis/roles/lead-pm.md, two fitness sets); initiative-check — 7 (incl. basis/glossary.md, basis/processes/product-flow.md); backlog-ordering — 4; stakeholder-presentation — 6 (incl. basis/artifacts/decision-brief.md, basis/processes/principle-set-authoring.md). lint_basis.py's 14 checks include "4. relative links resolve" but no status check on the target.

findings.claim: Every measurable word target in the corpus is missed by nearly every instance — this is not selective waiving, it is a constraint with a ~0% compliance rate.
findings.evidence: Against basis/guidelines/base-writing-style.md's target table: Features 18/18 over the 1,000-word target (median 4,350; max 17,030 — features/feat-tool-skills-rest.md). Process definitions 25/25 over the 800-word target (median 2,154; max 6,562 — request-intake.md). Decision records 18/18 over the 500-word target (median 2,092; max 4,152). Feature Document History rows 121/126 over the 25-word target (median 146, i.e. 5.8x; max 1,669 words in ONE row). Initiatives 7/16 over the typedef's 500-word rule. Guidance records 7/12 over 600.

findings.claim: The working principle set — the document compiled into every session — stands `approved` while its own fitness screen records that two judged screen rows claim passes an independent judge could not reproduce.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md §"Accepted tradeoffs" (line 307): "**The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce.** Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently." Also accepted there: "Three statement bullets carry two obligations each" (violates guideline rule 7 / fitness scenario 2) and "Three implications assert obligations their statements do not make" (violates rule 4 / scenario 4). Its own fitness scenario 5 requires "every claimed pass is one the judge can reproduce". Approved 2026-09-16 with verdict `tradeoffs-accepted`. All four principle-set fitness screens contain only the literal word "pass" in every cell.

findings.claim: `define-good-up-front` still mandates that "the check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability", while the two approved processes that produce the primary product artifacts both have the maker check its own work — the principle was left standing and the practice diverged under it.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md `define-good-up-front` bullet 3 (unchanged since seed commit 52b6e52), plus its implication "The same role never both performs and checks an activity — process definitions name both roles, so this is checkable mechanically." But feature-authoring.md v8: `draft` run-by lead-po, `self-check` run-by lead-po. adr-authoring.md: `author` and `record` both run-by lead-solutions-architect; basis/artifacts/adr.md states "authored, self-checked, and recorded ... no independent screen runs." The three processes that DID hold an independent cold-reviewer screen (initiative-check, po-output-check, stakeholder-presentation) are all now retired. No lint check compares maker and checker roles — the claimed mechanical check does not exist (lint_basis.py reads run-by roles only in derive_chain, line 780).

findings.claim: Half of all process steps are runtime routing and counter bookkeeping, not work: 110 of 207 steps are `execution: runtime`, and only 70 make anything.
findings.evidence: 25 process definitions, 207 steps total. By run-by: 110 runtime (53%), 77 agent, 10 human (4.8%), 10 sub-process. By function: 70 make (34%), 34 check/screen/verdict/approval (16%), 103 routing/counter/read-status/open-close (50%). Worst cases: product-flow 19 steps of which 13 runtime and exactly 1 makes anything (`more-features`, a judgment); request-intake 22 steps, 11 runtime, 12 non-make-non-check; small-change 17 steps, 11 runtime.

findings.claim: Check machinery is a smaller share of process mass than H2 predicts; the larger bulk is Document History and loop plumbing.
findings.evidence: Section word split across the 25 process definitions (50,177 words): Steps 33.9%, Document History 30.6%, Data block 17.0%, generated Flow diagram 9.8%, Derived checks 7.8%. Within step prompts: check steps 2,722 words vs make steps 6,611 (check share 29%). Of 481 declared step inputs, 179 (37%) are check/loop machinery names; `round`+`round_cap`+`round_log` alone are 46 (9.6%). Across the whole corpus (379,988 words of basis + working artifacts), Document History is 119,464 words — 31%.

findings.claim: The mandatory-check obligation is structural and inherited, not a misreading: the root `definition` typedef requires every definition to carry a closing checks section, and every principle set's admission bar requires each principle to imply at least one check.
findings.evidence: basis/artifacts/definition.md §Required sections 2: "A closing **checks section** (its heading contains 'check') — every definition implies at least one check; a definition no check can cite does not govern anything", with §Commitment citing `define-good-up-front`. 10 of 24 typedefs declare `definition` in ancestry and inherit it. Each principle set's opening carries "...and it implies at least one practice and one check" (principles.md:42, architecture-principles.md:69, implementation-principles.md:92, experience-principles.md:74), and each set's Fitness screen carries it as a mandatory row: "Implies ≥1 practice and ≥1 check (this document's intro)".

findings.claim: The authority's own correction against check-shifting produced one more mandatory check, not fewer — and the resulting principle amendment counted a route-acceptance as the owner's approval.
findings.evidence: requests/req-2026-09-05-maker-self-check.md §1 quotes the authority: "Reviews were always meant to be a safety check and define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks." The change made in response added a fifth MUST to `define-good-up-front`: "The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check, and record that it did." Acceptance statement 2 records the owner's approval as "standing on the product authority's ruling of 2026-09-05 accepting this request" — i.e. acceptance of the routing decision retro-counted as approval of the principle amendment at principle-set-authoring's `authority-approve` step. Seed text (git 52b6e52) had 3 obligations; it now has 5.

findings.claim: H3 is refuted for architecture and confirmed for implementation: the architecture set does state built-artifact properties, but neither set says anything about design or code craft — those words do not exist in the corpus.
findings.evidence: Statement-bullet classification: working set 22 of 26 bullets constrain an ACTIVITY (85%); architecture set 11 of 20 describe a BUILT-ARTIFACT property (55%) — `contracts-between-contexts` (3/3), `knowable-shape` (4/4), `local-comprehension` (3/4) are genuinely about the shape of the designed system; implementation set only 6 of 23 (26%), and all six concern scenario-conformance or records. Corpus-wide grep over basis/: "modular" 0 files, "cohesion" 0, "code quality" 0, "test coverage" 0, "idiomatic" 0, "coupling" 1, "inheritance" 1. Five of six implementation principles end in a "The checking role MUST fail..." bullet.

findings.claim: A guidance-style principle is mechanically excluded by four independent clauses, so the exclusion is over-determined and cannot be fixed by relaxing one rule.
findings.evidence: (1) basis/artifacts/principle-set.md §Required sections 2: the statement "is yes/no testable" — "use modular design" is not decidable on one piece of work. (2) basis/guidelines/principle-set.md rule 1 Criterion: "a reviewer can answer yes or no without reading the rationale or implications", with its Before example being exactly a guidance-shaped sentence ("Contracts matter and should generally be respected") presented as the rejected form. (3) basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md scenario 2: "every term the decision turns on is defined in the statement, the set's opening, or the glossary" — "modular" appears nowhere in basis/glossary.md. (4) scenario 6 (Lencioni): "the opposite rule is one an honest shop could adopt" — no honest shop adopts "use monolithic design". Plus the screen row "Implies ≥1 practice and ≥1 check".

findings.claim: H6 is half-wrong in a way that matters more than the hypothesis states: RFC 2119 keywords are deliberately confined to principle statements, but only the MUST tier is ever used — the corpus has zero graded obligations.
findings.evidence: Across the four principle sets: ~90 MUST/MUST NOT uses, ZERO uses of SHOULD (all four occurrences are the opening's keyword-definition mention), 6 real MAY uses. Outside the sets the keywords are absent by rule (guideline rule 2, "Confine normative keywords to statements"): basis/artifacts/feature.md, basis/guidelines/feature.md and basis/fitness/feature.fitness.md contain 0 MUST each. So the judgement-improving documents did NOT adopt BCP 14 — but the rule documents adopted only its hardest tier, and BCP 14's own discretion mechanism (SHOULD) is unused anywhere in the corpus.

findings.claim: H1's density claim is confirmed, but at the compilation step rather than in the prose: compiling principles into the session block raises obligation density sevenfold by stripping exactly the parts that make a rule interpretable.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md: 4,053 words carrying 26 obligations = 1 per 156 words, each with rationale and implications attached. .claude/shop/principles.md (compiled into every session): 537 words carrying 25–26 MUST = 1 obligation per ~21 words, with rationales, implications and the fitness screen removed by design ("The full set — rationales, implications, fitness screen — is the source document"). Total governed context at session start = 1,077 words (principles block 537 + primer 535 + name/type 2). Raw prose density is NOT the problem: mean sentence length is 18.5 words in processes, 17.3 in principle sets, 13.4 in typedefs — unremarkable.

findings.claim: H5 is confirmed but mislocated: the defined product flow contains exactly ONE product-authority step; the authority's actual load comes from the corpus-maintenance processes, i.e. from building the system rather than running it.
findings.evidence: Human steps total 10 of 207 across 25 processes. On the path request→built software, only three are defined: request-intake `confirm` and `observe` (both human: originator) and discovery-conversation `observe` (human: product-authority). feature-authoring, adr-authoring, scenario-assignment, implementation and reconcile-and-close have zero human steps. The authority's other six human steps sit in definition-chain-migration (2), principle-set-authoring, review-conversation, work-conversation — none on the product path. discovery-conversation's `observe` loop has NO round cap: its only exits are the authority's own "converge/close" or "cancel" classifications. Cost records: product-authority appears in 11 of 44 recorded step rows.

findings.claim: Two approved documents give contradictory homes for the same act — where the bet on an initiative is taken — with no reconciliation.
findings.evidence: basis/artifacts/initiative.md (approved) §Identity: "**Bet directly at discovery.** The authority bets on the initiative ... inside the discovery conversation's own human step ... with no separate check between framing and bet." basis/processes/initiative-check.md v12 still defines step `decide` — "Take the bet", run-by {role: product-authority, execution: human} — and is cited by basis/glossary.md, basis/guidelines/initiative.md and basis/fitness/initiative.fitness.md, all approved. Its only protection is a `status: retired` field that no check reads. Separately, the initiative word cap is stated twice with different values: basis/artifacts/initiative.md "At most 500 words" vs basis/guidelines/base-writing-style.md target table "Initiative | 400".

findings.claim: A draft process definition has a rendered skill sitting at the agent's load point, violating `governed-context` and skill-rendering's own enumerate rule.
findings.evidence: .claude/skills/implementation/SKILL.md exists with frontmatter `status: draft`; basis/processes/implementation.md is `status: draft` v1 (2026-09-17). basis/processes/skill-rendering.md step `enumerate` runs `grep -l '^status: approved' ${definitions}/*.md`, so the rendering process could not have produced it. `governed-context` requires everything loaded into an agent's context to "trace to an approved definition or a governed record". (The retired processes' skills WERE correctly removed from the load point — the rendering machinery works; this one was placed outside it.)

findings.claim: Roughly half of all required document sections exist to serve a check or an audit rather than a reader, and the audit half is the part that grew without bound.
findings.evidence: 24 typedefs demand 95 sections of their own instances, plus 34 inherited (10 definition-descended types inherit opening + checks section + Document History; 14 others inherit Document History) = 129 required sections. Classified as check/audit-serving: ~60 (~47%) — every Document History and checks section, plus Fitness scenarios / Derived review checklist / Commitment in the typedefs, plus instance sections that must be present even when empty (feature §Interaction types "always present ... or 'none' with the reason", §Edges coverage table, initiative §Feasibility and usability). Measured outcome: Document History is 27.6% of typedef mass and 30.6% of process-definition mass; 951 history rows and 649 cumulative versions across 115 basis files in 26 days = 5.6 amendments per definition.

findings.claim: The authority-facing channel breaches its own commitment in 7 of 10 cases, and the type says decisions made that way are not recordable as approvals.
findings.evidence: basis/artifacts/decision-brief.md §Commitment: "budgets hold (decision layer ≤ ~400 words, total ≤ ~1,500) ... **Consequence on failure:** ... decisions made from a failed brief are not recorded as approvals." Actual brief+annex totals: 030 1,966 · 032 1,826 · 034 1,700 · 035 3,381 · 036 3,599 · 037 3,417 · 038 2,045 — 7 of 10 over ~1,500; three within (031 849, 033 1,136, 039 1,372). The producing process (stakeholder-presentation) is retired, so the cold-read gate its Commitment cites (O3) no longer runs.

findings.claim: `feedback-loops-with-consumers` mandates that effectiveness be measured, but measurement exists for only a quarter of sessions and two of those files are empty.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md: "The effectiveness of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be measured" and "The definitions ... MUST be updated from what is measured." sessions/ holds 22 session records but only 7 `*-cost.md` files, of which 2 (sess-2026-09-09-b, sess-2026-09-17-a) contain zero rows. Total measured: 44 step rows, 2,716,421 tokens, 82.9 minutes — one session (sess-2026-09-07-b) accounts for 1,748,782 of those tokens across 7 rows. No measure of process outcome quality exists anywhere, only cost.

findings.claim: Sub-process nesting is shallow (max depth 3) and is not a source of complexity; the composition problem is that two different top-level processes both enter the same conversation.
findings.evidence: Deepest chain: product-flow → discovery-conversation → session-handoff = 3 levels. request-intake → discovery-conversation → session-handoff = also 3. Only 10 sub-process steps exist across 207. But product-flow's `discover` step and request-intake's `open-discovery` step both instantiate discovery-conversation-process with overlapping parameters, and request-intake's `land-outcome` and product-flow's `route-discover` then read the same initiative independently — two entry points, no stated precedence.

input.surprises:
WHAT I EXPECTED AND DID NOT FIND

1. I expected dense, convoluted prose. The sentences are fine. Mean sentence length is 18.5 words in process definitions, 17.3 in principle sets, 13.4 in typedefs — ordinary technical-writing numbers. H1's intuition is right about the symptom but wrong about where the density lives: it is created at the COMPILATION step, where 4,053 words of principle carrying 26 obligations become the 537-word block every session actually reads, at one hard obligation per 21 words with all rationale and implications stripped. The corpus solved its own verbosity problem by deleting the interpretable half.

2. I expected the check apparatus to dominate the process mass. It does not. Check steps are 16% of steps and 29% of prompt words. The bigger mass is elsewhere: 53% of all steps are `execution: runtime` routing and counter-advancing, and Document History is 31% of the entire corpus. The system spends more words recording that it worked than working.

3. I expected H3 to hold across both design sets. It does not hold for architecture — `contracts-between-contexts`, `knowable-shape` and `local-comprehension` are genuinely statements about what the built thing must be like (11 of 20 architecture bullets). It holds hard for implementation (6 of 23, all of them about scenario-conformance or records). What actually vanished is design CRAFT, and it vanished completely: "modular", "cohesion", "code quality", "test coverage" and "idiomatic" appear in zero files across all of basis/.

4. I expected H6 to be confirmed. It is half-refuted in an interesting way: the corpus deliberately BANNED RFC 2119 keywords from the judgment documents (feature typedef, guideline and fitness set contain zero MUST between them). But in the sets that do use them, it uses only the top tier — roughly 90 MUST, six MAY, and ZERO uses of SHOULD anywhere. It imported the coercive half of BCP 14 and discarded the discretion half.

5. The biggest thing none of the six hypotheses names: the flow has no receiver. No Bounded Context exists on this branch, no contract exists, and scenario-assignment has a recorded, unrepaired gap for assigning to the lead shop itself (bd lead-ki66p). Product-flow's entire second half — assign, dispatch, build, verify — is unreachable, and `implementation-process` is not a step of product-flow at all. This is a structural reason no software has been built that is completely independent of verbosity, check-density, or the authority's attention. A second restart that fixes only the writing would reproduce it.

6. The most damaging single artifact is the primer, not any definition. 535 words, loaded into every session, naming four RETIRED processes as the live flow — including "deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions", where that process is retired and nothing replaced it. 31 approved documents also cite retired processes. The lint cannot see any of it because its link check only verifies the file exists.

7. H4 is not a story about bad actors routing around rules. Every waiver I found is disclosed in writing, often eloquently — including basis/principles.md's own admission that its fitness screen "claim[s] passes ... that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently." The system's honesty is intact; its enforcement is not. The compliance rate against its own measurable targets is approximately zero (18/18 features, 25/25 process definitions, 18/18 decision records, 121/126 history rows all over), which means these are not constraints at all — they are aspirations with a recording obligation attached.

8. The self-check change is the sharpest single datum for the restart decision. The authority said checks had become a substitute for quality: "define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks." The system's response was to add a FIFTH mandatory obligation to `define-good-up-front` requiring makers to check themselves and record it — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, while leaving bullet 3 ("The check MUST sit with a different role") standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. The corpus's reflex under correction is to add a rule, and it has no reflex for deleting one.

No Bounded Context exists on this branch, no contract exists, and scenario-assignment has a recorded, unrepaired gap for assigning to the lead shop itself (bd lead-ki66p). Product-flow's entire second half — assign, dispatch, build, verify — is unreachable, and `implementation-process` is not a step of product-flow at all. This is a structural reason no software has been built that is completely independent of verbosity, check-density, or the authority's attention. A second restart that fixes only the writing would reproduce it.

6. The most damaging single artifact is the primer, not any definition. 535 words, loaded into every session, naming four RETIRED processes as the live flow — including "deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions", where that process is retired and nothing replaced it. 31 approved documents also cite retired processes. The lint cannot see any of it because its link check only verifies the file exists.

7. H4 is not a story about bad actors routing around rules. Every waiver I found is disclosed in writing, often eloquently — including basis/principles.md's own admission that its fitness screen "claim[s] passes ... that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently." The system's honesty is intact; its enforcement is not. The compliance rate against its own measurable targets is approximately zero (18/18 features, 25/25 process definitions, 18/18 decision records, 121/126 history rows all over), which means these are not constraints at all — they are aspirations with a recording obligation attached.

8. The self-check change is the sharpest single datum for the restart decision. The authority said checks had become a substitute for quality: "define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks." The system's response was to add a FIFTH mandatory obligation to `define-good-up-front` requiring makers to check themselves and record it — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, while leaving bullet 3 ("The check MUST sit with a different role") standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. The corpus's reflex under correction is to add a rule, and it has no reflex for deleting one.
